bug_info.bug_desc: The cache controller failed to protect a store hit against an outstanding miss that targeted the same cache index. In the STORE_REQ state it unconditionally wrote the store data to the hit way and returned to idle, with no re-check of MSHR aliasing between the tag-lookup cycle and the data-write cycle. In the WAIT_MSHR state it used only the full-address match signal (mshr_addr_matches_i) to decide when to retry, so an outstanding miss with a different tag but the same index was not treated as a conflict. The miss_handler likewise only exposed a full-address match, providing no index-only match output. As a result, a store could update a cache line that the miss handler was simultaneously evicting or refilling for a different tag at the same index, and the store update could be silently overwritten by the refill, corrupting cached data.
bug_info.fix_hint: Add an index-only MSHR match output in miss_handler that compares only the cache-index bits of each port's address to the outstanding miss address, and route it to cache_ctrl as mshr_index_matches_i. In cache_ctrl, guard the STORE_REQ write with this index match and transition back to WAIT_MSHR when an alias is detected. In WAIT_MSHR, wait for mshr_index_matches_i to clear before re-requesting the tag lookup, so a store hit is deferred until no outstanding miss targets the same index.
